thread:
sophie (Support): FYI — Customer AcmeCorp opened a ticket: AWS Marketplace invoice line items don't match Redwood dashboard totals for Feb. They see $2,347 on AWS but our usage dashboard shows $1,890. They also reported different token counts (AWS shows ~12M, our dashboard ~9.8M). Can someone help triage?

lee (Finance): Thanks. Do we have the customer's AWS invoice PDF and the marketplace line item IDs? Also need the payer account ID (consolidated billing can add confusion).

customer: AcmeCorp: attaching screenshot of AWS invoice and our dashboard export. AWS line: "Redwood Inference - usage (us-east-1)" $2,347.59, line item id: li-0a1b2c3d. Dashboard CSV attached shows 1,892.40 USD and token_count 9,843,210.

ben (Eng-Platform): First pass: Marketplace exports often report gross charges (including marketplace fees / taxes) and sometimes use a different meter (calls/requests vs tokens). We need three exports: (1) Redwood usage CSV (per-hour or per-day) for Feb, (2) AWS Cost & Usage Report line items for the same timeframe, (3) marketplace metering reports (if available). Can you upload the raw CSVs?

billing-bot: Daily usage export ready: https://internal-exports.redwood/apps/usage/2026-02. Use token-level CSV: redwood-usage-2026-02.csv

lee (Finance): Also check if they have a Reserved/Committed Capacity contract applied — marketplace will bill usage plus any reserved commit or surcharge. Tara, did this account have a Reserved/Dedicated commit?

tara (Account Exec): AcmeCorp has a Dedicated reserved commitment (monthly), but they routed billing through AWS Marketplace for convenience. Marketplace invoices include a marketplace fee (~10%) and currency conversion rounding in some months. That alone can explain part of the delta but not 20%+ token mismatch.

ben (Eng-Platform): Repro steps I recommend we run (internal):
```
# grab Redwood CSV for date range (already in billing-bot link)
curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_SERVICE_KEY" \
  "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/usage?start=2026-02-01&end=2026-02-28&format=csv" -o redwood-usage-2026-02.csv
# sum tokens (token_count column)
awk -F, 'NR>1 {sum += $4} END {print sum}' redwood-usage-2026-02.csv
# pull AWS Cost & Usage Report filtered by LineItemId
aws s3 cp s3://acmecorp-cur/2026/02/lineitems.csv .
grep "li-0a1b2c3d" lineitems.csv > aws-li-0a1b2c3d.csv
awk -F, '{tot += $n} END {print tot}' aws-li-0a1b2c3d.csv  # replace $n with cost column index
```
Follow up: ensure we use the same timezone and billing period boundaries. AWS uses UTC by default in CUR, Redwood uses customer time zone unless overridden.

sophie (Support): Good point about timezones. Customer said their billing window is Feb 1–28 UTC; I confirmed the dashboard export was generated with UTC too.

ben (Eng-Platform): Another potential mismatch: marketplace might be reporting "meter quantity" as number of requests (API calls) not token units. If an integration uses embeddings heavy calls the meter can be per-embedding-unit instead of tokens. Ask customer: are they using embeddings heavily in Feb?

customer: AcmeCorp: yes we spiked embeddings mid-Feb for a reindex (lots of small calls). We expected token counts to go up, but AWS shows an even bigger jump.

lee (Finance): Action items: 1) customer to upload full AWS invoice PDF + CUR snippet (we need line item granular rows). 2) Support to verify which SKU/meter the marketplace line corresponds to (subscription vs usage). 3) Eng to run the reconcile script and map APIs -> meter id -> tokens. 4) Finance will open a case with AWS Marketplace ops if we confirm marketplace misattribution or double-counting.

ben (Eng-Platform): I'll run a quick recon and post results. Preliminary hypothesis: marketplace fee + meter type mismatch + rounding -> ~10–15% diff; remaining delta likely because CUR line aggregates multiple meter IDs under one description string. I'll try to match the CUR product code/usageType fields to our internal meter IDs.

billing-bot: Export generated: s3://internal-exports/reconciliation/acmecorp/2026-02-recon-ready.tar.gz

tara (Account Exec): I'll message the AWS partner ops contact once we have the mapping file. If there's a reserved commit, we should be able to show that the marketplace applied reserved pricing incorrectly (seen that once before).

sophie (Support): Thanks. AcmeCorp — could you upload the full CUR extract and attach your AWS payer account ID in the ticket? That will let us ask AWS to trace line item li-0a1b2c3d. Also please confirm whether the embedding spike was single large batch jobs or many small calls — that changes how tokens vs calls are reported.

customer: AcmeCorp: uploading now. The spike was 1 big reindex job split into 1500 small embedding calls over 2 days. Upload: acme-cur-Feb.zip, invoice-2026-02.pdf

lee (Finance): Received. I'll start an internal ledger reconciliation and post the CSV. If we confirm marketplace added the 10% fee line as a separate charge that isn't in our dashboard, we can explain that to them and show adjusted totals. If AWS mis-tagged meter IDs we'll escalate.

ben (Eng-Platform): Update (later): matched 98% of tokens after mapping CUR usageType->redwood_meter_id and normalizing token vs call meters. Remaining ~2% due to marketplace rounding and tax. Putting the mapping CSV in the ticket.

sophie (Support): Great — I'll paste Ben's mapping and Lee's adjusted invoice to the customer and close loop. :thumbsup:

customer: AcmeCorp: thanks — that mapping explains it. Please add a note to our billing so future invoices include an itemized breakdown. Appreciate the fast help. :clap:

sophie (Support): Closing here after customer confirmation. If anything else pops up we can re-open.
